title: totalBudget()/runwaySeconds() view inconsistency persists and uses pre-accrual rewardBudget
description:
`totalBudget()` returns `rewardToken.balanceOf(this) + dispatcherHook.mintDebt()`, while `runwaySeconds()` uses `rewardBudget + dispatcherHook.mintDebt()` divided by `rewardRate`. These two quantities disagree: `rewardToken.balanceOf(this) = rewardBudget + totalDebt + any forfeited/dust` and NOT equal to `rewardBudget` alone. Additionally, neither view projects `_updatePool` accrual that hasn't been settled yet — so `rewardBudget` in `runwaySeconds` may still contain seconds of about-to-be-accrued emissions.

The inconsistency means that `totalBudget` over-reports the deployable budget (it includes already-earmarked user debt), while `runwaySeconds` under-reports (it uses a rewardBudget that hasn't been settled for elapsed time).
impact: View-only; monitoring dashboards and any keeper logic that multiplies `runwaySeconds * rewardRate` and compares to `totalBudget` will never reconcile. No funds at risk.
proof: Deploy, fund the pool, let a staker accrue some rewards over time without claiming, then read both views. `totalBudget()` includes the staker's accrued-but-unclaimed rewards (part of `balanceOf(this)` but not part of `rewardBudget`); `runwaySeconds()` uses `rewardBudget` which excludes them. The two figures disagree by `totalDebt`.
suggested-fix: Make the two views use congruent accounting: either both use `rewardBudget + dispatcherHook.mintDebt()` (exclusive of earmarked debt), or both use `balance + mintDebt` (inclusive). Add NatSpec clarifying the semantics. For `runwaySeconds`, project `_updatePool` first (like `pendingReward` does for the per-share accumulator) so the runway reflects current-instant accrual, not stale state.
